final.memo:
Charlie and I have reviewed the business and have decided to pass. While the company holds insurance and retirement franchises of significant scale, the business's true economic position is obscured by opaque financial guarantees and credit-default-swap portfolios [D01, D05].

We cannot assess the moat or the economics when the ultimate cash requirements in a stress scenario are unbounded [D01]. The company reported a $13.16 billion net loss for the first six months of the year, a figure that highlights the severe instability within their current risk portfolios [D01].

Management has promised to review every business, but as owners, we require a clear view of the underlying assets and liabilities before committing capital [D01]. We have no interest in guessing the potential for permanent loss when the collateral requirements remain unknown [D01].

Intrinsic value is incalculable in this environment [D03]. We prefer to hold cash and T-bills, waiting for opportunities that we can actually understand, rather than risking Berkshire's capital and reputation on a situation that belongs firmly in our "too hard" pile [D01, D08].
